the audit risk assessment process, as well as the audit risk assessment model, is a critical component to the audit process, and that the audit risk model is a useful tool to auditors in assessing the risk of material misstatement of an entity s financial statements.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the auditor confidence in management’s plausible explanations is a critical factor in determining the risk of material misstatement and the level of evidence required.
auditors tend to be overconfident in management’s explanations of the causes of the misstatement.
the use of professional judgment by auditors is an important aspect of the audit process, but it can be negatively affected by cognitive biases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

auditors do not appear to have a consistent approach to reassign risk, and that the reassignment of risk is not necessarily based on the auditor s confidence in the management s explanations for the identified risks.
the auditor s assessment of management s plausibility is an essential part of the auditor risk assessment.
auditors are not immune to heuristics and cognitive biases that affect decision making.
